questions.question_text: Parallelogram $P$ has a base of $18\text{ cm}$ and a perpendicular height of $5\text{ cm}$. Parallelogram $Q$ has a base of $15\text{ cm}$ and a perpendicular height of $6\text{ cm}$. Which has the larger area?

options.why: Paired $Q$’s base with $P$’s height, calculating $15\times5$.
Paired $P$’s base with $Q$’s height, calculating $18\times6$.
Added the base and the height for each shape instead of multiplying them.

questions.solution_text:
$A_{P}=18\times5$
$=90\text{ cm}^{2}$
$A_{Q}=15\times6$
$=90\text{ cm}^{2}$
Neither is larger: both parallelograms have an area of $90\text{ cm}^{2}$.
